newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - Colombian premiums ease.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - Colombian premiums ease.

text.p: Colombian differentials showed signs of softening this week on the New York physical coffee market, but spot business remained sluggish despite a sharp downturn on the CSCE futures market, traders said.
"Nobody needs spots," said one trader. "Business is just dead. Roasters are going back to the just-in-time mode."
"Colombians are cheaper this week," he added. "But they are not able to sell."
Spot Colombian MAMs were heard at 20 to 22 cents over "C" versus 25-28 cents a week ago. MAMs for October-December shipment continued to net 18 cents over December.
Elsewhere, spot Bolivian coffee garnered eight cents over "C", while spot Peruvian beans fetched 10 to 11 cents over "C"
Prime Mexican beans, also on the spot market, netted four to five cents over "C" and November forward primes were heard at four cents under December ex warehouse Laredo.

Talk on the physical market revolved around rumors that some coffee is being moved from European warehouses to U.S. exchange warehouses for certification against the board. No coffee has appeared yet, but traders said roasters' fears about tight supply have subsided as it gets closer to the new-crop harvest in many Latin American countries in the Fall.
"Roasters don't believe in this market," said one trader. "Why build inventory when a lot more coffee is coming in the next two or three months?"

Also easing supply concerns was the Green Coffee Association of New York stock data for July. After the close on Friday, GCA reported supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses rose in July by 219,000 60-kg bags, to 2,335,000 bags.
CSCE September coffee fell 6.60 cents a lb Friday to settle at 177.95. December ended 4.20 cents lower at 161.85.
